original_question: Which occurrence is rarer: ectrodactyly in FAES syndrome or ectrodactyly occurring independently of FAES?

final_qi.question: How rare is ectrodactyly in FAES syndrome?
final_qi.long_answer: Within FAES syndrome, split-hand/split-foot malformation (ectrodactyly) has only been described in isolated, single-case reports.  Consequently, it is regarded as an exceptionally uncommon—i.e., extremely rare—manifestation of the syndrome.

final_qi.question: How rare is ectrodactyly occurring independently of FAES?
final_qi.long_answer: Isolated ectrodactyly (split hand/foot malformation) is exceedingly uncommon. Epidemiologic data show it occurs in roughly one out of every 90 000 live births, whereas most other cases appear as part of syndromes such as the facio-auriculo-ectodermal spectrum (FAES). Thus, ectrodactyly occurring independently of FAES is extremely rare.
